Maryland Climate Vulnerability Score

Source: R/data.R
climate.Rd

Tract-level values going into the state Department of the Environment's Climate Vulnerability Score. Similar to EJSCREEN, the score scales risks of environmental hazards based on vulnerable socio-economic populations. The subset of data here just includes tree canopy cover, urban heat islands, drought risk, and flood storm surge, plus the overall score percentile.

Usage

climate

Format

A data frame with 1463 rows and 6 variables:

geoid

Character. The tract FIPS code.

tcc

Numeric. Tree canopy coverage as a percentage of land area that is tree canopy.

drought

Integer. Ranking of area and intensity of drought conditions, with higher numbers as more severe risk.

uhi

Integer. Presence of urban heat island compared to other parts of the same city, with higher numbers as more severe heat.

flood_ss

Integer. Ranking of historical and predicted flood storm surge impacts, with higher numbers as higher risk.

cvs_pctl

Numeric. Percentile of tract-level Climate Vulnerability Score.

Source

Maryland iMAP Data Catalog. MD Climate Vulnerability Score, available at https://data.imap.maryland.gov/datasets/maryland::md-climate-vulnerability-score. See methodology at https://mde.maryland.gov/programs/air/Climate-in-md/Documents/Climate%20Vulnerability/CSNA_%C2%A7_1-702_Methodology_1.5.pdf

Examples

 head(climate)
#>         geoid   tcc drought uhi flood_ss cvs_pctl
#> 1 24003731103 0.667       3   1        3     7.66
#> 2 24003707001 0.624       3   2        3    17.78
#> 3 24003740800 0.497       3   1        4    44.19
#> 4 24003702402 0.588       3   1        4    25.03
#> 5 24003731303 0.694       3   1        3     8.55
#> 6 24003730603 0.589       3   1        3    22.85
